title: India's Women Archers Stun China for World Cup Gold
excerpt: Deepika Kumari, Ankita Bhakat, and teenage sensation Kumkum Mohod beat hosts China in a nail-biting shoot-off in Shanghai.
body:
Deepika Kumari, Ankita Bhakat, and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod delivered one of Indian archery's most electric moments on Sunday — defeating hosts China in a shoot-off to claim gold at the Archery World Cup Stage 2 in Shanghai.

**What Happened — a Comeback for the Ages:**
The fourth-seeded Indian trio beat a young second-seeded Chinese team 28-26 in the shoot-off after both sides were locked at 4-4 through four regulation sets. Seventeen-year-old Kumkum Mohod opened the decisive shoot-off with a perfect 10, setting the tone for the team. With an 8 needed to seal the win, four-time Olympian Deepika shot a 9 to complete the victory.

**Why This Gold Matters:**
This win secures India's first Archery World Cup gold medal since 2021. It also marks Deepika's 39th Archery World Cup medal, Ankita's eighth, and Kumkum Mohod's first. The road to gold was equally remarkable — India had defeated 10-time Olympic champions and top seeds South Korea 5-1 in the semi-finals. Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya saluted the team on X, writing: 'Golden Grit, Fearless Spirit, Podium Finish! Heartiest congratulations to Deepika, Ankita, and Kumkum for clinching Gold at the Archery World Cup Stage 2.'

**What to Watch Next:**
India concluded the Shanghai leg with two medals overall, adding Sahil Jadhav's bronze in the men's individual compound event. The next stage of the Archery World Cup circuit will be the key test of whether this resurgent Indian women's recurve unit can sustain its momentum into the Olympic qualification cycle.
